original_question: In every k-blocked point set, must each color class contain at most k points?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 5 in Section 2.4 of arXiv:1012.5187, not the broader bounded-size Conjecture 3. The survey explicitly attributes this question to Aloupis et al.; in the original research paper Blocking Coloured Point Sets (arXiv:1002.0190), the same question appears as Conjecture 29 in Section 6.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical content of the per-colour-class conjecture: it asks universally about every k-blocked point set, and it uses the correct proposed upper bound, namely k points in each colour class. It also stays narrower than the paper's main bounded-total-size conjecture, which is the right scope here.
missing_details: Specify that k is a positive integer and that the object is a finite set P of points in the Euclidean plane R^2.
Define what it means for a point x to block two distinct points v and w: x must lie in the interior of the segment vw.

Define k-blocked precisely: each point of P is assigned one of k colours, and for distinct v,w in P, v and w have the same colour if and only if some other point of P blocks v and w; equivalently, v and w are visible with respect to P if and only if they have different colours.
Clarify that a colour class means the subset of points receiving a fixed colour.

If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, clarify whether unused colours are allowed; the paper's formulation says 'assigned one of k colours', so the cleanest phrasing is simply 'every colour class' (or 'every nonempty colour class' if one wants to avoid ambiguity).
Make clear that this is the later stronger per-colour-class conjecture, not the main conjecture that only asks for some bound on the total size of a k-blocked set.
refined_question: For every positive integer k, if P is a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane together with an assignment of one of k colours to each point such that, for any distinct points v,w in P, the points v and w receive the same colour if and only if there exists a third point x in P lying in the interior of the segment vw (equivalently, v and w are visible with respect to P exactly when they receive different colours), must every colour class of P contain at most k points?
justification: The draft matches the paper's per-colour-class conjecture almost verbatim. In the survey arXiv:1012.5187, this is Conjecture 5 in Section 2.4, stated immediately after the definition of k-blocked point sets and the two basic lemmas about collinearity and general position. The survey attributes the conjecture to Aloupis et al. In the original source paper Blocking Coloured Point Sets, the same question is stated as Conjecture 29 in Section 6, after the formal definition of k-blocked sets in Section 1. Because your draft clearly targets this later conjecture, it should not be replaced by the broader main conjecture that every k-blocked set has bounded total size. I therefore only added the missing definitions needed to make the question self-contained and paper-faithful.
